description.narrative: Inclusive, low-carbon, and environmentally sustainable development in Ningbo promoted

At least 3 million local residents (at least 40% women) benefited from pollution reductions through improved municipal solid waste management Progress/Status: Municipal solid waste collection, transport, recycling, and sorting subprojects in Zhenhai District and Cixi City are estimated to benefit ~2.4 million residents. Female beneficiaries estimated at 51%, exceeding the minimum gender threshold. Data Source: Project reports (semiannual, annual), or records of NMG and the three financial intermediaries Target value: 3 million Actual value:

At least 750,000 tons of carbon dioxide emissions reduced annually Progress/Status: The two operational subprojects quantified reductions constitute about 136,800 tons CO2/year.
1. Ningbo Heshengda Energy Technology Co., Ltd. project (thermal energy comprehensive utilization project of Ningbo SK Synthetic Rubber Co., Ltd.) achieved 58,106 tons CO2/year reduction based on energy savings of 23,652 tce and national conversion factors.
2. Ningbo Heshengda Energy Technology Co., Ltd. project (waste heat recovery renovation project for the heating furnace flue gas in the hot rolling plant of Ningbo Iron & Steel Co., Ltd.) achieved 78,700 tons CO2/year reduction based on 29,160 tce equivalent waste heat recovery. Data Source: Project reports (semiannual, annual), or records of NMG and the three financial intermediaries Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity in climate mitigation and green financing strengthened Indicator: At least 200 women entrepreneurs report increased understanding and knowledge of ESG through trainings organized by the project management office and Ningbo Women Entrepreneurs' Association Progress/Status: The service providers delivered the structured, multi-stage training aligned with international ESG disclosure standards, alongside expert-led workshops on green finance, low-carbon transition, and climate-related policies. It incorporated practical case studies, peer learning, and interactive sessions to strengthen understanding of climate finance instruments, regulatory requirements, and enterprise-level implementation approaches. The activities also established a multi-stakeholder platform linking government, financial institutions, enterprises, and international experts to facilitate knowledge exchange and support coordinated green and low-carbon development. The capacity buildings on ESG reporting, new low-carbon technologies, and climate financing have been provided to 30 women entrepreneurs.
On 14 October 2024, IFS, ISSB Beijing Office, and IFRS Foundation Beijing Office provided training on green finance and transition finance for FIs, roadmap for development of green banks, introduction to IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and sustainability disclosure empowering enterprises to over 150 participants from enterprises, financial institutions, and government agencies on 14 October 2024, including 47 women, which accounted for 23.5% of the target number.
Data Source: List of attendees, survey of the participants Actual value:

Data Source: Annual reports of the three financial intermediaries Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity in climate mitigation and green financing strengthened Indicator: At least one national policy recommendation on cold energy recovery developed and submitted to relevant government authority for issuance Progress/Status: The consultant, China Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Industry Association, started working in November 2024. The final report and policy recommendation were concluded in October 2025. The report reviewed the policy measures and current practices of LNG cold energy recovery and utilization in Japan and the Republic of Korea, assessed the current status in PRC, and analyzed the key challenges and barriers to its development.
Policy recommendations proposed: (i) to strengthen top-level policy design and integrated planning by embedding LNG cold energy utilization into national and regional strategies, aligning LNG receiving terminals with downstream industrial development, and ensuring coordinated, safe, and efficient deployment; (ii) to establish an enabling policy and market framework by ensuring stable LNG supply, introducing targeted fiscal, pricing, and green finance incentives, and recognizing LNG cold energy as a form of green energy eligible for carbon markets and supportive tariffs; and (iii) to accelerate technological innovation and scale-up through R&D investment, demonstration projects, industrial collaboration, and strengthened international cooperation to close efficiency gaps and unlock large-scale low-carbon benefits. Data Source: Government and financial intermediary reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity in climate mitigation and green financing strengthened Indicator: Disclosure of the first ESG report in the PRC following IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 standard of the International Sustainability Standards Board by at least one of the financial intermediaries in 2025 Progress/Status: The TRANSFINTECH supported the Bank of Ningbo on developing a benchmarking table of sustainable information disclosure requirements, an analysis report on the differences between the ISSB Standards and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange guidelines, a sustainable information disclosure template, and an analysis of challenges and recommendations for implementing the ISSB Standards. 2024 Bank of Ningbo Sustainability (ESG) Report which is consistent with the IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 standards of the ISSB, was disclosed in December 2025. Data Source: Government and financial intermediary reports Actual value:

Output: Digital carbon accounts for large industrial emitters established Indicator: A digital platform established with energy usage and carbon emissions data from major industrial emitters Progress/Status: Initial progress has been made. The mission discussed the proposed digital carbon account platform and agreed to broaden its scope from a traditional carbon-inclusive platform to a comprehensive citywide carbon management system. The platform is expected to support carbon accounting, carbon footprint tracking, ESG disclosure, transition finance verification, carbon-performance assessment, and green finance data services. The entity to lead implementation will be assigned by the Ningbo government. Data Source: Project reports (quarterly, semiannual, annual) Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: Not Established Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: Not Established Target year: 2030 Target value: Established

Output: Digital carbon accounts for large industrial emitters established Indicator: Carbon account rating system established Progress/Status: The carbon account rating system is still under development. The mission agreed that the platform should support carbon-performance assessment and provide data services to facilitate green lending and investment decisions. Further work is needed to define the methodology, align it with emerging national requirements and international disclosure standards, and ensure data security and public-sector oversight. Data Source: Project reports (quarterly, semiannual, annual) Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: Not Established Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: Not Established Target year: 2030 Target value: Established
